I planned the same Christmas trip twice. Once by hand. Once by handing everything to an AI agent. Same dates, same budget. Let's see who does better.

Quick difference first. A chatbot answers from what it knows. An agent actually acts: it opens the websites, searches, compares, and does the math.

By hand, a trip like this means picking a destination, comparing flights, finding hotels for every budget, halal restaurants, holiday opening hours… and adding it all up. Five websites, and a pile of tabs.

So I gave the agent one mission. Leave from Paris, December twenty-sixth to thirty-first. Find the cheapest destination, and build three plans: solo, couple, and family.

It opened Google's price map and scanned the whole of Europe. The cheapest: Manchester. Sixty-six euros return. Then it caught the trap: that flight leaves from Beauvais, with no cabin bag. From Charles de Gaulle, it's ninety-two.

And it spotted a tip I always scroll past. Leave on the twenty-seventh instead, and the flight drops to forty-one euros.

Then hotels, on Booking, with filters. Solo: a room rated eight point six, two hundred and twenty-eight euros for five nights. Family: an apartment rated nine point two, four hundred and fifty meters from the center, and the kids stay free.

It mapped the halal restaurants around the center. And for holiday opening hours, I asked an AI assistant with web search. It flagged a library that was closed for the entire holiday last year, and dropped it from the plan.

So where does AI beat manual planning? It tests more combinations, it spots hidden fees, it checks opening hours, and it does all the math for you.

Now, the honest part. That same assistant admitted its hotel prices were only estimates: it couldn't open the booking sites. The agent could. Some websites push back against agents. And neither of them books or pays for anything. You check, you decide.

The result: three complete plans, at five hundred, one thousand, and twenty-five hundred euros. Would you let an AI book your next trip?
